concepts.name: Three-Dimensional Solids
concepts.description: Three-dimensional (3D) solids occupy space and have measurable dimensions such as length, breadth, and height. Common solids include cubes, cuboids, cylinders, cones, hemispheres, and spheres.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify common three-dimensional solids and describe their basic characteristics.

concepts.name: Surface Area and Volume
concepts.description: Surface area measures the total area covering the outer surface of a solid, while volume measures the space enclosed by the solid.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to distinguish between surface area and volume and identify appropriate units for each.

topics.title: Surface Area of a Combination of Solids

concepts.name: Combined Solids
concepts.description: Many practical objects are formed by joining two or more basic solids. Their surface area is determined by considering only the exposed surfaces.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify composite solids and determine their total surface area.

concepts.name: Calculation of Surface Area
concepts.description: The surface area of a composite solid is calculated by adding the surface areas of the individual solids and subtracting the common contact surfaces when necessary.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to calculate the surface area of combined solids using appropriate formulas.

concepts.name: Applications of Surface Area
concepts.description: Surface area calculations are used in painting, polishing, packaging, and material estimation for three-dimensional objects.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to solve real-life problems involving the surface area of composite solids.

topics.title: Volume of a Combination of Solids

concepts.name: Volume of Composite Solids
concepts.description: The volume of a composite solid is obtained by adding or subtracting the volumes of its component solids depending on the structure of the object.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to calculate the volume of composite solids using standard volume formulas.

concepts.name: Volume Formulas for Standard Solids
concepts.description: Standard formulas for cubes, cuboids, cylinders, cones, hemispheres, and spheres provide the basis for calculating the volume of more complex objects.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to apply appropriate volume formulas for different three-dimensional solids.

concepts.name: Applications of Volume
concepts.description: Volume calculations are essential in determining storage capacity, material requirements, liquid capacity, and engineering measurements.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to solve practical problems involving the volume of combined solids.

concepts.name: Key Concepts of Surface Areas and Volumes
concepts.description: This chapter summarizes methods for calculating the surface area and volume of individual and composite three-dimensional solids using standard geometric formulas.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to select appropriate formulas and accurately calculate the surface area and volume of composite solids in mathematical and real-world contexts.
